mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has risen each of the last three weeks (-53.0 to -46.0), indicating a steady return of commuting activity. This sustained momentum should continue to lift incidental retail visits tied to commute routines, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -53.0 to -46.0 over three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase on average over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend for at least three more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has been declining steadily (21.1 to 18.1) as people spend less time at home. Once RESIDENTIAL drops below a 17.5-point threshold, reduced at-home time should translate into materially higher discretionary outings, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 17.5 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 21.1 to 18.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of RESIDENTIAL crossing below 17.5, or RETAIL_REC falls despite the threshold breach.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both risen together over the last three weeks (WORKPLACES -53.0 to -46.0; TRANSIT -66.0 to -61.0). Their joint recovery signals a compounding return-to-routine effect that amplifies retail footfall beyond what either series would produce alone, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than what a single-series (WORKPLACES-only or TRANSIT-only) model would predict, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent sustained improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT suggests an active loosening of mobility restrictions. In a reopening regime, this policy relaxation should directly permit higher retail and recreation activity, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -66.0 to -61.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines even as WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to improve, indicating restrictions are not actually easing or retail is excluded from relaxation.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS shows high week-to-week volatility (e.g., -2.7 to 18.3 to -2.6), consistent with early-spring weather swings. When PARKS spikes more than 15 points above the prior week, favorable weather is likely drawing people to outdoor recreation instead of indoor retail, temporarily suppressing RETAIL_REC the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -2.7 to 18.3 then fell back to -2.6 within two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not dip the week following a PARKS spike greater than 15 points, or rises instead.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has risen substantially (-19.7 to -12.6), suggesting essential-trip demand is normalizing rather than spiking defensively. As essential-trip urgency fades, households reallocate outings toward discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -19.7 to -12.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite continued GROCERY_PHARM improvement, suggesting no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES crossing above the -45 threshold would indicate a formal policy milestone (e.g., office reopening order) that triggers a step-change increase in associated retail foot traffic near business districts, raising RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above -45 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -46.0 in the most recent week, approaching the -45 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show a step increase in the four weeks after WORKPLACES crosses -45, or the crossing does not occur within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-spring reopening regime with improving weather (evidenced by volatile but net-positive PARKS readings) alongside rising WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, outdoor and work-related mobility substitutes for indoor retail activity, keeping RETAIL_REC flat or slightly suppressed over the next week even as other sectors recover.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and WORKPLACES both show upward movement across recent weeks while RETAIL_REC remains roughly flat around -63
regime_hint: early spring reopening with improving weather
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in lockstep with PARKS and WORKPLACES rather than remaining flat or declining, indicating no substitution effect.
